lines.text: do i have to die again
cry the biggest cry oh when
will the last straw break it all
and i can't even make amends
cause nothing that is left makes any sense
i can hear the cracking of my sternum
holding back a heart that never quits
rising from the ashes of inferno
the cosmos in just a single bit
paradox's ugly face has begun to grow on me
it nothing short of the truth
i am boiled alive in all these feelings
boiled, reduced till there is nothing left
whatever i expected to be healing
this is all but more and infinitely less

n1.body:
a deep realization is in a way the death of an old version of oneself
there is a point where this death is feared, and a point where it becomes desired relief
to be very clear - i am NOT idealizing suicide here, but using the metaphor of death as a prelude to metaphorical rebirth within one lifetime.

n2.body:
what has been held back for many years cannot be any longer
it rushes forth with overwhelming force

n4.body:
after the pain of letting go passes, there opens a world of wonders
a simple clarity and freedom

n5.body:
holding paradoxes is a high art
transcending the belief everything has a single answer liberates

n6.body: a grape needs to be crushed to become wine

n7.body: where i thought i need to do more, the answer often tends to be do less
